newsitem.title: USA: NAPM's Kauffman says manufacturing prices steady.
newsitem.headline: NAPM's Kauffman says manufacturing prices steady.

text.p: An official from the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) characterized as steady the overall price picture in the manufacturing sector of the economy, depite a near four-point jump in manufacturing prices in September.

Speaking to reporters in a teleconference after the NAPM released its monthly report on manufacturing, Ralph Kauffman said, "I would say it's fairly steady right now. We are seeing some increases in some areas; a lot of them seem to be related to oil and natural gas input."
Kauffman is chairman of the NAPM business survey committee.
As for growth in manufacturing, Kauffman said factory owners may wish to grow at a slightly more rapid pace, but he noted that they are aware of the risks of too much growth.
"I think they might like a little bit more growth, but they are aware of problems that would come from too much growth," Kauffman said.
Going forward, Kauffman said future indicators point to continued steady growth in manufacturing near term.
"I think continued steady growth at approximately the level we've seen recently is probably indicated for the very near term," he added.
Steady growth near term would continue a trend that has been in place over the past six months.
Kauffman said it would be fair to characterize manufacturing growth over the last half year as "steady."
"Our index has kind of fluctuated a bit up and down, but all within the range indicating growth," he said.
Turning to the backlog of orders index in September, Kauffman said that component hinted that production will not fall dramatically over the short haul.
"I think what it (the backlog of orders index) says is that production is not going to drop drastically," he said.
The NAPM's index slipped to 51.7 in September from 52.6 in August. Prices were up almost four points to 51.2.
